newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch clear up 'hidden' copper mystery.
newsitem.headline: Dutch clear up 'hidden' copper mystery.

text.p: The Dutch Statistical Office admitted Wednesday that it had supplied flawed data on flows of copper through Rotterdam, clearing up a puzzle over "missing" stocks of the metal that threw world markets into disarray.

Import and export figures that the Statistical Office supplied to the World Bureau of Metal Statistics last month seemed to indicate that more than 500,000 metric tons of copper was lying hidden in Rotterdam warehouses.
A Bureau of Metal Statistics report drew this conclusion after comparing the Dutch figures with official London Metal Exchange data.
The report was largely rejected by traders and analysts but the theory, coming in the wake of the Sumitomo trading scandal, still rattled the market and sent world copper prices tumbling.

The Statistical Office said Wednesday that the inaccuracies in its data completely explained how the WBMS had drawn its conclusion. "The amounts fully match up," a spokesman said. "This accounts for the copper."
The main reason for the problem, it said, was a failure to distinguish between copper imported into the Netherlands for domestic use and copper passing through the country in transit.
